I am 63 years old and have worked this land since I was 13. I never went to school, but my hands and eyes have learned everything over 50 years. My farm is 4.1 mu here in Quzhou County, just enough for my household of two. We grow winter wheat and summer maize, the same wheat-maize rotation that everyone on the North China Plain has done for generations.

My wheat is already in the ground—it went in last October after we rotary-tilled the field. Now it is waking up from the winter. I will irrigate it three times from our well: once when it greens up, once at the jointing stage, and once when the grain is filling. I will topdress with urea when the wheat turns green—about 30 jin per mu—and I put down compound fertilizer at the base to give it strength. The wheat seeds are the improved kind from the seed station. They are not the old traditional seeds; they grow stronger and resist the rust better. I will spray herbicide once in early spring to kill the weeds, and I will spray two more times for insects and disease before harvest. If the weather is fair, I expect about 900 jin per mu.

When we harvest the wheat in early June, we will immediately plant summer maize. We do not till the soil again—we plant directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage, which saves time and keeps the moisture in the ground. Everyone here uses hybrid maize seed now, like Zhengdan 958 or Denghai. I will spread compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress with urea when the maize is knee-high. I will irrigate twice: once when the plants are growing tall, and once at tasseling when the ears are setting—that is the critical time. Two sprays on the maize: herbicide at planting, and insecticide for corn borer. I hope for about 1,100 jin per mu.

I do not read books and I do not use computers, but I know this land. I watch the sky, I listen to my neighbors, and I use what my well can give me.
